original_value: Social networking is an interactive Internet of Things. The symmetry of the network can reflect the similar friendships of users on different social networks. A user’s behavior habits are not easy to change, and users usually have the same or similar display names and published contents among multiple social networks. Therefore, the symmetry concept can be used to analyze the information generated by the user for user identification. User identification plays a key role in building better information about social network user profiles. As a consequence, it has very important practical significance in many network applications and has attracted a great deal of attention from researchers. However, existing works are primarily focused on rich network data and ignore the difficulty involved in data acquisition. Display names and user-published content are very easy to obtain compared to other types of user data across different social networks. Therefore, this paper proposes an across social networks user identification method based on user behavior habits (ANIUBH). We analyzed the user’s personalized naming habits in terms of display names, then utilized different similarity calculation methods to measure the similarity of the features contained in the display names. The variant entropy value was adopted to assign weights to the features mentioned above. In addition, we also measured and analyzed the user’s interest graph to further improve user identification performance. Finally, we combined one-to-one constraint with the Gale–Shapley algorithm to eliminate the one-to-many and many-to-many account-matching problems that often occur during the results-matching process. Experimental results demonstrated that our proposed method enables the possibility of user identification using only a small amount of online data.

result.paraphrase: Social networking is an interactive form of the Internet of Things. Network symmetry can reveal similar friendships among users on different social networks. Because user behavior habits are difficult to change, users often have the same or similar display names and posted content across multiple social networks. For this reason, symmetry can be used to analyze user-generated information for identity identification. User identification is essential for constructing better social network user profiles, so it has important practical value in many network applications and has attracted extensive attention from researchers. However, existing studies mainly concentrate on rich network data and overlook the difficulties of data collection. Compared with other user data across social networks, display names and user-posted content are much easier to obtain. Accordingly, this paper proposes an across social networks user identification method based on user behavior habits (ANIUBH). We first analyzed users’ personalized naming habits through display names, then applied different similarity calculation methods to measure the similarity of the features contained in those names. Variant entropy values were used to assign weights to the features above. In addition, we measured and analyzed users’ interest graphs to further improve identification performance. Finally, we combined a one-to-one constraint with the Gale–Shapley algorithm to remove the one-to-many and many-to-many account matching problems that often arise during result matching. Experimental results showed that the proposed method makes user identification possible using only a small amount of online data.
